body:
Every support conversation can win or lose a customer. How well the AI or human agent on the other end of the interaction listens and solves the problem decides which route the call takes. In isolation, one conversation may not seem like much. Added up across every call and chat, they decide whether a business keeps its customers or keeps replacing them.

According to a Zendesk study , more than 50% of customers switched to competitors after a single bad experience. That shows the importance of customer service skills, even as AI continues to disrupt CX operations. Organizations that continuously upskill their CX team have a competitive advantage as customer expectations grow.

This guide explores key customer service skills, why they matter for businesses, how to improve them, and how AI augments CX teams.

## Summary

• Customer service skills help businesses solve customer problems, build trust, and reduce customer churn.

• Generally, CX teams practice hard and soft customer service skills, including communication, problem-solving, and conflict resolution.

• Both human and AI agents can apply customer service skills through planned rollout, conversational evaluation, and refinement to improve customer experience.

• While AI agents can help with conflict resolution, a seamless handoff to human agents is critical for de-escalation.

• When deploying AI agents for customer service, evaluate conversational metrics during training and after deployment to drive continuous improvement.

## What are customer service skills?

Customer service skills are the soft and technical abilities that help a support team understand customer needs and resolve their problems effectively. These skills are broadly categorized into soft skills, like communication, patience, empathy, and adaptability, and technical skills, like product knowledge or incident management.

We’ll explore seven of these skills in more detail: communication, problem-solving, conflict resolution, empathy, adaptability, personalization, and product knowledge. We’ll also touch on how each one applies to both human and AI customer support agents.

## Customer service skills, explained

Customer service skills are practices that help customer experience teams actively listen, understand, respond, resolve, and follow up on customer issues. These skills draw on practices from different disciplines, spanning communication, problem-solving, empathy, and conflict resolution. Equipping your team with the right customer service skills ensures a consistent, positive customer experience across all touchpoints.

Traditionally, support teams develop customer service skills through training in both soft and hard skills. For example, you learn how to pause and listen, note customer frustration, and use respectful words to de-escalate situations. In addition, CX teams must be familiar with tools such as CRM and ERP to surface information during conversations. Increasingly, employees in CX need a high level of tech literacy to work with AI agents to surface relevant information and expedite solving the customer’s issue.

In fact, the vast majority of customer service teams now use AI agents to streamline customer experience workflows. According to Gartner, at least 70% of customers will start their customer journey using an AI interface by 2028.

Upskilling the CX team remains important, but architecting AI support agents around brand SOPs, security guardrails, knowledge base integrations, and third-party tools is key to unlocking the potential of AI-powered CX operations.

## Why customer service skills drive better experiences

Effective customer service speeds problem resolution, driving brand loyalty, retention, and revenue over time. Instead of waiting for incidents to escalate, CX teams proactively investigate customer-reported cases. They listen actively and give customers space to share their thoughts before then helping to resolve any problems or queries.

The same applies to AI customer service agents . Even though they’re driven by generative AI, machine learning, and other software technologies, you architect them around workflows, principles, and policies that build trust. Whether AI, humans, or both, your goal is to resolve customers’ problems and make them feel heard.

When integrating AI into CX workflows, Jannes Koopmann, Sr. AI Business Owner at 3Shape , stressed the importance of an empathetic tone and a human-like feel. As his company modernized customer support with AI agents, Jannes wanted to ensure customers feel understood throughout the entire process.

## The 7 customer service skills every human and AI agent needs

Good customer service requires both humans and their AI counterparts to be competent across different skills. These are the skills needed for customer service, with examples of how human and AI agents apply each one.

## Communication skills: Listen actively and speak clearly

Clear communication prevents confusion, which causes customers to abandon calls or messages when seeking help. Communication skills require active listening, concise responses, and clear written and verbal communication.

Human agents develop communication skills by listening to what customers say and choosing appropriate words in response. They avoid jargon for clarity and always clarify technical terms, whether in email, on a call, or via text.

AI agents, particularly those powered by LLMs, excel at conversational responses. However, AI agents need specific guidelines for turn-taking and handling interruptions. For example, when a customer pauses mid-speech, a voice agent must respond within a specific window to sound natural. At the same time, it mustn’t talk over the caller or give unrelated answers.

Both human and AI agents can communicate better when they share conversation context effectively. This means that AI and the CX team must have real-time access to conversational analytics to respond accurately.
